the quark-antquark pair creation effects are essential for a quantitative description of the mass shifts, and that they are responsible for the mass shifts of the baryons in the vicinity of the threshold.

the mass shifts of the octet and decaplet baryons are small and negative, with the exception of $\Lambda(1520)$ and $\Sigma(1670)$, which show positive mass shifts.

our unquenched QM calculation of the mass-shifts of the octet and decaplet baryons, which includes $q\bar {q}$qq¯pair creation effects explicitly, is able to reproduce the experimental data with a remarkable precision, thus confirming the reliability of the quark model as a tool for describing hadronic observables.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the coupling of baryon resonances to mesons is the main source of baryon mass shifts, whereas the coupling to baryon resonant states is of minor importance.
the coupling to the continuum leads to a mass reduction of the baryons, and the mass shift is of the order of 50 MeV for the nucleon, and 100 MeV for the $\Sigma$ and $\Lambda$ hyperons.
the mass shifts of all the baryons are positive and that the mass shifts for the baryons with the lowest masses (N, $\Delta$) are the smallest.

the coupling to the continuum is a significant effect for the octet and decaplet baryons.
